documents.title: H&P - Admission - COPD Exacerbation
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 04:40, HD1
Chief complaint: 3 days of worsening SOB and cough productive of yellow sputum.
HPI:
73M with known GOLD 3 COPD, ex-smoker 50 pack-years, quit 8 yrs ago, presents with progressive dyspnea.
Baseline: walks 1 block before stopping, no home O2. Now dyspneic at rest, 2-pillow orthopnea unchanged from baseline.
Sputum increased in volume and changed from clear to yellow over 48h. Subjective chills, no measured fever at home.
Used home albuterol MDI q2h overnight with minimal relief. No chest pain, no hemoptysis, no calf pain.
2 prior COPD admissions in past 18 months, no prior intubation.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Mild accessory muscle use noted at triage, resolved after first nebulizer; respiratory rate 22.
Two albuterol nebulizers in the ED with improved air movement; patient ambulating in hallway before admission decision.
Ipratropium neb x1, methylprednisolone 125 mg IV x1 given in ED.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Discussed with attending; admit to stepdown telemetry for close resp monitoring.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
COPD, GOLD 3
HTN
Type 2 DM, diet controlled, last A1c 6.4
Hyperlipidemia
BPH
Remote appendectomy
HOME MEDICATIONS:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h PRN
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly
ALLERGIES: penicillin - rash
SOCIAL: lives with wife in single-story home. Son local. Independent ADLs. No alcohol. No current tobacco.
FAMILY HX: father with emphysema.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: positive for dyspnea, cough, sputum, fatigue. Negative for fever, N/V, dysuria, rash, edema.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Vitals 04:30 - T 37.1, HR 96, BP 142/84, RR 22, SpO2 91% on 4L NC.
Gen: elderly male, alert, speaking in short phrases but improved, no distress at rest.
HEENT: mucous membranes dry, no JVD.
Chest: barrel chest, decreased breath sounds bilaterally with diffuse expiratory wheeze, prolonged expiratory phase. No focal crackles.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur. No peripheral edema.
Abd: soft, nontender, BS present.
Ext: no calf tenderness, no cyanosis, trace clubbing absent.
Neuro: A&Ox3, no asterixis, follows commands.
DATA:
Na 137, K 4.1, Cl 99, CO2 32, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 128.
Trop neg x1. BNP 62.
CXR: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms, no infiltrate or effusion.
ECG: sinus tach 98, no acute ischemic changes.
ASSESSMENT:
73M with acute exacerbation of COPD, likely infectious trigger, with acute on chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure.
PLAN:
Duoneb q4h scheduled, albuterol q2h PRN.
Steroid: prednisone 40 mg by mouth daily, tolerated without hyperglycemia. Start this AM after ED IV dose.
Doxycycline 100 mg BID x5 days given PCN allergy.
O2 via NC titrate to SpO2 88-92%, avoid oversaturation.
Repeat ABG or VBG in 4-6h; continuous pulse ox and telemetry.
Hold nothing else; continue home lisinopril, atorvastatin, tamsulosin.
Fingerstick glucose q AC and HS while on steroid.
Incentive spirometry, ambulate with RN assist, SCDs for VTE ppx (heparin 5000 SC q8h ordered).
Pulmonary consult in AM. Code status: full, confirmed with pt and wife.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 AM
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:20
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports breathing easier overnight. Slept in 3 blocks, woke twice with cough. Sputum now lighter in color, less volume.
Used 1 PRN albuterol at 02:10 for wheeze, relief within 15 min. No chest pain, no fevers.
Ate most of breakfast. Ambulated to bathroom with RN without desaturation.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.9, HR 84, BP 134/78, RR 18, SpO2 92% on 2L NC (weaned from 4L at 05:00).
I/O 1100/1350. Weight stable.
Gen: comfortable, speaking full sentences.
Chest: improved air movement, scattered end-expiratory wheeze, no accessory muscle use.
CV: RRR, no murmur, no edema.
Neuro: alert, oriented, no asterixis.
CBG this AM 118 and 132 - no hyperglycemia on steroid.
WBC down to 10.4. Cr 0.9, K 4.0.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
COPD exacerbation, improving. Hypercapnia trending down.
1. Continue duonebs q4h, PRN albuterol q2h.
2. Continue prednisone 40 mg PO daily, day 2 of 5.
3. Doxycycline day 2 of 5.
4. Wean O2 to keep SpO2 88-92%; trial room air with ambulation today.
5. PT eval for gait and endurance.
6. Continue heparin SC, incentive spirometry q1h while awake.
7. Restart home inhalers today, review technique with RT.
Pulmonary saw pt, agrees with plan, will follow.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD5, 08:05
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt says he feels near baseline. Walked the hallway loop twice yesterday PM and once this AM without stopping.
Cough much reduced, sputum clear and scant. No nocturnal awakenings last night. Appetite good.
Asking about going home; wife present at bedside.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.8, HR 78, BP 128/72, RR 16, SpO2 93% on room air at rest.
Ambulatory pulse ox 10:? - RN documented walk at 07:45, SpO2 nadir 90% on RA, no dyspnea.
Gen: well appearing, no distress.
Chest: good air entry bilaterally, rare faint expiratory wheeze at bases, no accessory muscle use.
CV: RRR. Abd soft. Ext no edema.
CBG 104, 126, 119 over past 24h - steroid tolerated without hyperglycemia.
Basic metabolic panel unremarkable, CO2 29, Cr 0.9.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
COPD exacerbation, resolved to near baseline. Off supplemental O2 since HD4 09:00.
1. Off scheduled nebs, switched to home inhalers with spacer; RT confirms adequate technique.
2. Prednisone day 5 of 5 - last dose today, no taper needed.
3. Doxycycline completes today.
4. PT cleared pt for home, no DME needed.
5. Plan discharge HD6 AM if stable overnight on room air.
6. Counsel on action plan, when to call, smoking abstinence reinforced.
7. Arrange pulmonary follow-up and consider pulm rehab referral at discharge.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - COPD Exacerbation
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit HD1, discharged HD6 at 11:15. Total LOS 6 days.
Discharge diagnosis: acute exacerbation of COPD with acute on chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Secondary: HTN, T2DM diet controlled, hyperlipidemia, BPH.
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
73M with GOLD 3 COPD presented with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and purulent sputum.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Mild accessory muscle use noted at triage, resolved after first nebulizer; respiratory rate 22.
Two albuterol nebulizers in the ED with improved air movement; patient ambulating in hallway before admission decision.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Treated with scheduled duonebs, doxycycline x5 days (PCN allergy), and systemic steroids.
Oral steroid: prednisone 40 mg by mouth daily, tolerated without hyperglycemia. Completed 5-day course HD5.
Oxygen weaned from 4L to 2L on HD2 and to room air HD4 09:00.
Repeat VBG HD2 pH 7.34, PaCO2 55. WBC normalized from 13.2 to 8.1.
CXR showed hyperinflation without infiltrate. Trop and BNP unremarkable.
PT evaluated and cleared for home; ambulated hallway loops on HD5 with SpO2 nadir 90% on RA.
No arrhythmia on telemetry. Fingersticks ranged 104-132 throughout stay.
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE: stable, ambulatory, SpO2 93% on room air, RR 16.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily - resume
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID - resume
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h PRN with spacer
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly
No further prednisone or antibiotics - both courses completed inpatient.
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care in 7 days.
Pulmonary clinic in 2-3 weeks; referral placed for pulmonary rehabilitation.
PATIENT INSTRUCTIONS:
Use inhalers with spacer daily, rinse mouth after steroid inhaler.
Return for increasing breathlessness at rest, colored sputum with fever, confusion, or inability to speak full sentences.
Remain tobacco free. Annual flu and pneumococcal vaccines discussed.
Discharge instructions reviewed with pt and wife; both verbalized understanding.
